messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The testInfiniteLoop test triggers an infinite loop in HelpFormatter when printing help for a command line with an option that has a very long description. The failure is described as an infinite loop due to line wrapping in HelpFormatter.printHelp.

The test calls printHelp on a HelpFormatter instance with a width set to 20 and options that include a long description. The current bug report confirms that if a word is longer than the available wrapping width, the wrapping code goes into an infinite loop until the JVM crashes.

Tracing through the method calls:
- printHelp(String, Options) calls printHelp(int, String, String, Options, String, boolean) with default widths and settings.
- That method uses a PrintWriter to call printHelp(PrintWriter, int, String, String, Options, int, int, String, boolean).
- This calls printOptions(PrintWriter, int, Options, int, int) to render option descriptions.
- printOptions calls renderOptions(StringBuffer, int, Options, int, int).
- renderOptions generates formatted option strings including descriptions and calls renderWrappedText to wrap descriptions to the given width with indentations.
- renderWrappedText tries to wrap the text by repeatedly finding wrap positions and appending lines.
- The infinite loop bug occurs inside renderWrappedText in the while loop starting at line 822.
- If findWrapPos returns the same position as the previous wrap position (pos == lastPos), it means the text is too long to wrap correctly, causing the loop to stall.
- Instead of handling this case gracefully, the method throws a RuntimeException with message "Text too long for line - throwing exception to avoid infinite loop [CLI-162]: " + text.
- However, this exception is not handled higher up, resulting in the older code hanging (possibly because this exception was added recently).
- Before the exception was added, the code likely ended up in an infinite loop because the wrap position did not advance and the while loop kept retrying.

Therefore, the root cause is the inability of renderWrappedText to handle words longer than the wrapping width. The method findWrapPos finds no suitable break and returns the same position repeatedly, causing an infinite loop. The fix should be to detect and break out of this loop or handle very long words differently inside renderWrappedText.

Recent issue reports are not relevant as they describe other parsing and argument handling issues.

The buggy method is:
HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(StringBuffer, int, int, String)

Other relevant methods are:
HelpFormatter.printHelp(...)
HelpFormatter.printOptions(...)
HelpFormatter.renderOptions(...)

The test reproduces the problem by using a description longer than the width, exercising the word wrapping code in renderWrappedText.

The infinite loop happens in the while(true) loop of renderWrappedText because the wrap position doesn't advance when a word is too long.

The addition of the RuntimeException "Text too long for line" is a protection to avoid infinite loop which was likely added later.

In summary, the bug occurs because HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText does not handle very long words correctly for wrapping; the loop fails to progress and loops infinitely.

This matches the current bug report's description and the failing test reproduces the issue exactly.

The fix involves improving renderWrappedText to correctly handle words longer than the width and avoid infinite loops.

This is the diagnosis based on the source, test, and bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
